modules.title: Introduction to Early Nigerian Cultures
modules.html:
The Nok, Ife, Benin and Igbo-Ukwu cultures and their art and achievements. This section covers introduction to early nigerian cultures.

Key points

  • The Nok culture, discovered in central Nigeria, is famous for its early mastery of _____. — iron smelting.
  • The first European power to establish a permanent presence on the Nigerian coast was _____. — Portugal.
  • The first Nigerian political party, the NNDP, was founded in 1923 by _____. — Herbert Macaulay.
  • The first Nigerian to be appointed a Bishop of the Anglican Church was _____. — Samuel Ajayi Crowther.
  • The Nigerian leader who introduced the 'Indigenization Decree' (1972) was _____. — Yakubu Gowon.

Worked examples

Q: The Nok culture, discovered in central Nigeria, is famous for its early mastery of _____.
A: iron smelting — Nok culture is globally recognized for being one of the earliest West African societies to develop iron-smelting technology and terracotta sculptures around 1000 BC.

Q: The first European power to establish a permanent presence on the Nigerian coast was _____.
A: Portugal — The Portuguese were the first Europeans to reach the Bights of Benin and Biafra in the late 15th century, establishing trade in ivory and slaves.

quiz.q: The Nok culture, discovered in central Nigeria, is famous for its early mastery of _____.
quiz.solution: Nok culture is globally recognized for being one of the earliest West African societies to develop iron-smelting technology and terracotta sculptures around 1000 BC.

quiz.q: The first European power to establish a permanent presence on the Nigerian coast was _____.
quiz.solution: The Portuguese were the first Europeans to reach the Bights of Benin and Biafra in the late 15th century, establishing trade in ivory and slaves.

quiz.q: The first Nigerian political party, the NNDP, was founded in 1923 by _____.
quiz.solution: Herbert Macaulay, often called the 'Father of Nigerian Nationalism,' founded the Nigerian National Democratic Party to contest elections in Lagos.

quiz.q: The first Nigerian to be appointed a Bishop of the Anglican Church was _____.
quiz.solution: Crowther, a former slave, was consecrated in 1864 as the first African Bishop of the Niger Territory.

quiz.q: The Nigerian leader who introduced the 'Indigenization Decree' (1972) was _____.
quiz.solution: General Gowon's decree aimed to give Nigerians greater control of the economy by restricting certain businesses to indigenous owners.

quiz.q: The 'Treaty of Union' (1961) involving Nigeria, Ghana, and Guinea was an early attempt at _____.
quiz.solution: Leaders like Nkrumah and Azikiwe were strong proponents of Pan-Africanism, seeking to unite newly independent African states.

quiz.q: The principal architect of the Nigerian Action Group (AG) party was _____.
quiz.solution: Chief Obafemi Awolowo founded the AG as a regional party for the Western Region.

quiz.q: Which Nigerian leader was assassinated in the February 13, 1976, abortive coup?
quiz.solution: General Murtala Muhammed was killed in an ambush led by Lt. Col. Bukar Suka Dimka.

quiz.q: The first Nigerian Prime Minister was _____.
quiz.solution: Balewa led the federal government from 1957 until his death in 1966.

quiz.q: The Nigerian leader who introduced the 'Indigenization Decree' of 1972 was _____.
quiz.solution: The decree aimed to give Nigerians greater control over the economy by restricting foreign ownership in certain sectors.

quiz.q: Which Nigerian leader is often referred to as the 'Zik of Africa'?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Nnamdi Azikiwe.

quiz.q: The British annexed Lagos in 1861 primarily to _____.
options: suppress the slave trade and protect commerce
quiz.solution: Lagos was annexed to ensure the end of the trans-Atlantic slave trade and to secure British interests in the palm oil trade.

quiz.q: The 'Satiru Rebellion' of 1906 was a challenge to British rule in _____.
quiz.solution: The Satiru uprising near Sokoto was a Mahdist movement against British occupation and their local allies.

quiz.q: The 1922 Clifford Constitution applied only to _____.
quiz.solution: The North was excluded from the Legislative Council under Clifford; the Governor ruled the North by proclamation.

quiz.q: The founder of the Mali Empire was:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Sundiata Keita.

quiz.q: The ancient Benin Kingdom is famous for:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Bronze casting.

quiz.q: The Policy of Assimilation was practiced by:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: France.

quiz.q: Who was the Head of the Interim National Government?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Ernest Shonekan.

quiz.q: The Benin Empire was famous for its:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Bronze works.

quiz.q: The Igbo society was historically:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Acephalous/Decentralized.

quiz.q: The Almoravids invaded Ghana Empire in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: 1076.

quiz.q: The Organization of African Unity (OAU) was formed in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: 1963.

quiz.q: Kanem-Borno was near:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Lake Chad.

quiz.q: Clifford Constitution year:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: 1922.

quiz.q: Berlin Conference year:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: 1884-1885.

quiz.q: ECOMOG is peace force of:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: ECOWAS.

quiz.q: Lagos was formally annexed by the British in...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: 1861.

quiz.q: The 1976 Local Government Reform made the Local Government the ___ tier of government.
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Third.

quiz.q: The Aro Confederacy was a dominant force in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Eastern Nigeria.

quiz.q: The capital of Ghana Empire was:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Kumbi Saleh.

quiz.q: Who was the 'Lion of Mali'?
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: Sundiata Keita.
